---
title: Devices
description: How an app keeps a copy of someone's data on a phone or a Mac, works without a connection, and sends its changes when it can.
---

A **device** is a program that keeps a **working copy** of part of an instance on the machine it runs on. It reads from that copy, and puts its writes in a **queue** that it sends when it can reach the server.

An app built on the [Swift SDK](/swift-sdk) is a device, and so is the [CLI](/cli)'s `marfa device`. A device syncs only with the instance, never with another device, because the instance is the [source of truth](/build/how-marfa-works#the-instance).

## The working copy

A device chooses the **slice** it keeps: the types, the tier and the edge types it holds. `*` alone holds every type except `system.*`. It can also **pin** an item to keep it whatever the slice says.

The device fills its copy once, by a **hydration** that reads every item in the slice, then keeps it current from the instance's [event stream](/build/events):

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa device --db reading.db hydrate --type core.bookmark --tier library
marfa device --db reading.db catch-up
```

```text
hydrated 1 item(s) and 0 edge(s) of core.bookmark at library in 1 page(s); cursor 32
applied 0 event(s), skipped 0; cursor 32
```

</Terminal>

Reads need no connection, [saved views](/build/read-a-view#read-a-view-from-a-working-copy) included. **While the copy fills, it answers from what has arrived**, marking a list or a search `partial`. An edge read or write, and a read or write of an item that hasn't arrived, are refused `hydration_incomplete`. A fill that stops partway resumes where it stopped.

Each item in the copy answers `read_only` as the server last gave it. Nothing announces a change to it, so once 15 minutes have passed the device asks again after a catch-up or while following, and reports the items whose value moved as `read_only_held`.

A second process can open the copy to read, with `--reader`: it's told each time the writer saves, and never writes.

### Tables and files

**A device holds a [table](/build/tables) only when an app asks**, with `marfa device tables hold` or the SDK: a phone can hold a step counter without ten years of its readings. A held table is kept whole up to 100,000 rows and 64 MiB, and past that its reads go to the server. Rows are kept current from `rows.changed`, and a follow tells the app `table.filled` once a table is whole.

A device keeps the files it fetched within a **file budget**, removing the ones read longest ago, as [Keep files on a device](/build/keep-files-on-a-device) shows.

## When the copy falls behind

A copy sometimes needs filling again, and its **queued writes wait** for the fill.

- **After a device was away longer than the instance keeps events**, its copy is `stale`. It answers reads, marking lists and searches `stale`, until a hydration refills it in place.
- **When another instance answers at the address, or the credential's reach changed**, the copy has expired. It refuses reads and writes until a hydration, which empties it first.

## A write made offline

A write made offline shows in the copy at once, and waits in the queue with the version it was based on. Sending the queue is a **drain**. A drain that can't reach the server leaves the writes where they are, and one that can sends them in order. The instance recognizes a retry, so it never applies a write twice. Each answered write gets a verdict, and the copy takes what the instance now holds.

A device sends every update with `conflict=auto`, so the instance settles most collisions, as [Versions](/build/versions#when-two-apps-write-the-same-item) explains.

## Verdicts

Each settled write gets one of six verdicts:

| Verdict | What happened |
| --- | --- |
| `accepted` | The instance applied the write. |
| `merged` | The write collided with another change to the same field, and the type's merge rule settled it. |
| `conflicted` | The write collided, and the type's merge rule put its value in a conflicted copy. |
| `refused` | The instance refused the write, whose content is kept to offer back. |
| `blocked` | Something must change before the write can go. |
| `dead` | The write failed five times, not counting lost connections, timeouts, rate limits or server errors. |

Only the last three need an **app's attention**. A `blocked` write says why:

| Reason | What clears it |
| --- | --- |
| `credential_refused` | A credential with the access it needs |
| `key_spent` | A release |
| `ancestor_unavailable` | A withdrawal, or a release once the credential can read the write's base version |
| `conflict_unresolved` | A withdrawal |
| `failing_alone` | A release or a withdrawal |
| `instance_changed` | A release, to the new instance, or a withdrawal |
| `awaiting_dependency` | Nothing: the answer to the write it waits for |

A **release** sends the write again in the next drain, under a fresh idempotency key. A **withdrawal** takes it out of the queue and puts the copy back to what the instance holds. `marfa device release`, `marfa device withdraw` and the Swift SDK's [queue](/swift-sdk/queue) do these. [Write in a working copy](/build/write-in-a-working-copy) shows each from the CLI.

A working copy can also be **a folder**, where each item is a file, such as a note in Markdown. [Sync a folder](/use/sync-a-folder) explains how.

The rules behind this page are in the [device](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/device.md), [queue and verdicts](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/queue-and-verdicts.md) and [folder sync](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/folder-sync.md) chapters of the contract.
